data.narrative:
Heliux is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Alex Craig and Victor Jakubiuk that has raised $4.7M to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector includes 11 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the seed-stage cohort remains tightly constrained for direct valuation benchmarking.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $5M and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. This reflects the expected value progression at institutional round close. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while 11 same-sector companies exist (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI), filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded insufficient datapoints to support a reliable median, rendering broad sector aggregation unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with $12M as the central estimate. This reflects a single methodological pillar and limited peer depth at the seed stage. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-set comparable data, which constrains conviction; the applicability of standard 2.5x stage-step multipliers to this specific founder team and market; and whether $5M raised serves as an appropriate valuation proxy given any secondary market signals or investor composition. Validation through additional private seed rounds or narrative-driven diligence is warranted.
